order_description: Respiratory assist device, bi-level pressure capability, without backup rate feature, used with noninvasive interface, e.g., nasal or facial mask (intermittent assist device with continuous positive airway pressure device)

candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: The order is for E0470, a bi-level device without backup rate, and the patient's qualifying diagnosis is mild obstructive sleep apnea (AHI 14, nadir 81%, no central or hypoventilation findings). L33718 is the policy that governs E0470 for OSA. L33800 covers E0470 for restrictive thoracic disorders, CSA/CompSA, hypoventilation, and COPD-related chronic respiratory failure, and it refers OSA E0470 coverage to L33718. Under L33718, E0470 requires that an E0601 CPAP was tried and proven ineffective, and the chart shows only a CPAP order (E0601) with no trial yet, so the E0470 order would not currently meet coverage. L33405 is a polysomnography policy that does not govern device coverage.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: Dr. Irene779 Kirlin939, the treating practitioner, saw the patient in person on 2026-03-12 for evaluation of possible obstructive sleep apnea (R152), before the attended in-laboratory polysomnography on 2026-03-23 (R50). Section II applies criteria A-C to the E0470 order.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test that meets either (1) AHI or RDI >= 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or (2) AHI or RDI >= 5 and <= 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of a. excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia, or b. hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: The AHI is 14 events/hour, which fails alternative 1 (below 15). Alternative 2 applies: the AHI is within 5-14, the 91 recorded events exceed the minimum of 10, and excessive daytime sleepiness is documented (Epworth Sleepiness Scale 17 in R102; patient dozing off while reading and watching television in R152). Alternative 2b is not needed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: R81 documents instruction on use and care of a CPAP device by a DME supplier on 2026-04-09. The record names CPAP rather than the E0470 bi-level device that was billed, and the 2026-04-05 note (R153) describes an E0601 order. This mismatch is noted but the instruction is treated as PAP device instruction.

criteria.policy_text: An E0601 has been tried and proven ineffective based on a therapeutic trial conducted in either a facility or in a home setting.
criteria.explanation: The record shows no E0601 therapeutic trial. The CPAP/E0601 order was placed on 2026-04-05 (R44, R153) and supplier instruction was given on 2026-04-09 (R81). The device has only just been prescribed, so no trial could have shown ineffectiveness. This contradicts the requirement for a failed E0601 trial before an E0470 is covered.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: An attended in-laboratory polysomnography (Type I, facility-based) was performed on 2026-03-23 and reported on 2026-03-25 with AHI, total sleep time and SpO2 nadir. Nothing in the record suggests the study was invalid.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test results (AHI 14 with 91 events over 6.5 hours of sleep) meet the AHI 5-14 pathway with documented excessive daytime sleepiness, as analysed under I.B.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: Dr. Irene779 Kirlin939 ordered the attended polysomnography on 2026-03-12 (R43), and the same practitioner documented 'Ordered a sleep study' in the 2026-03-12 note (R152).

decision_explanation: Criteria I.A, I.B, I.C, Sleep Tests.1, Sleep Tests.3 and Sleep Tests.4 are met, but II.D is not met. An E0470 requires that an E0601 was tried and proven ineffective, and the record shows the CPAP/E0601 was only ordered on 2026-04-05 and instructed on 2026-04-09 with no trial. Under the policy, an E0470 without criteria A-D met is denied as not reasonable and necessary.
